_comment: Candidate products for the October 2026 re-decision. Every goods/freight/duty figure here is an ESTIMATE from research, not a supplier quote, and duty is the weakest number in the whole model because the HTS classification is unresolved. Replace a row's numbers the moment a real quote lands. See 06-research-october.md part 7 and sheets/post-deminimis-scenarios.csv.

_shared._note: Costs that do not depend on which product is chosen.

candidates.name: Gua sha set, single @ $42
candidates.note: The current plan. Kitsch sells a steel gua sha at $12.99 on Amazon and $27 in Target, so the durability angle is category-standard copy, not a differentiator.

candidates.name: Gua sha set, 2-pack @ $69
candidates.note: Same product, bundled. The $0 change that most improves the odds: shipping amortises across units, so CM% holds while break-even CAC nearly doubles.

candidates.name: Pickleball paddle + attach @ $95
candidates.note: Best economics found. 24.3M US players in 2025, +22.8% YoY; core crush and delamination are a live, newsworthy complaint. BUT: a differentiated paddle needs MOQ 300 at $12.50-28.50 = $3,750-8,550, which this capital cannot reach, and the buyer is the most spec-literate in the set.

candidates.name: Hard-water shower filter + refill @ $84
candidates.note: Best fit for the existing audience research. Search +1,033%; Jolie did ~$50M in 2024 from one SKU at $148-169. The only candidate with a built-in consumable, so it has LTV rather than one-and-done. Goods cost is an estimate, not a quote.

candidates.name: Silk pillowcase set @ $79
candidates.note: Blissy did $7.65M in September 2024 alone at an ~$88 AOV, which proves the price point works on Meta. But the premium is pure brand, and brand is what $2,000 cannot buy.
